name: Bird's-foot trefoil
note: Bird's-foot trefoil, Lotus corniculatus: a low sprawling mat of small leaves with clusters of yellow pea flowers, tipped red in bud, then pods splayed like a bird's foot; food for the common blue butterfly and for bees. How it spreads: each plant sprawls from a deep taproot, its stems lying out across the turf, and does not root as it goes; it spreads by seed, the ripe pods twisting open in late summer and flinging seed a few meters. So it grows as many small mats scattered over the sandy turf rather than one bed. In the game: a mat widens about a meter every four or five days in spring and summer and rests in winter; seeds start new mats up to five meters off often through summer, less in autumn. A mat: a cover plant (recipes/world/growth.json cover), so a share per square meter rather than plants one by one (src/world/growth/cover.js matHour), drawn as a low carpet of stacked shells (mat-shells.wgsl, src/render/passes/mats.js). A machair plant of the meadow islet (B3a, Matt's pick of October 31, 2026): it comes only with the islet, planted as clumps on its turf when it rises (recipes/land/meadow-islet.json starters), never volunteers and is not in the Plant tool, so it stays the islet's own. habitat: shoreM is height above mean sea level; sand the painted sand share. growth: each square fills ratePerH of the gap toward how well the mat likes the ground each game hour, times seasonRate [spring, summer, autumn, winter] (it rests in winter). spread: planted (only ever planted, so its map is absent until the first clump); it creeps only into a square beside one at least fromShare full; with chance jumpPerH an hour, times jumpSeason (seed is set after flowering), a seed lands 2 to jumpM meters off a stand (jumpTries landings tried) and starts a patch jumpStart of full where the ground suits it at least jumpMinSuit; plantStart is how full a planted square starts; shadedBy lowers its target where the painted turf is thick (grass shades it out); grassYield is how much the grass gives way where it is full. Mats share the ground: one never grows past the room the others leave, and the first to hold a square keeps it. mat (the look, findable scale, about 1.5 times real): heightM the carpet's height at full cover; leafM the size of one leaf clump in the pattern; flowerM the size of a flower spot and flowerShare how many of the top spots flower while in flower (flowering, in season units 0 spring .. 4); edgeM the size of the wobble at a patch's edge; farTint how much its flowers tint it far off while in flower (from above it reads as a drift of their color); flowerR a flower head's radius as a share of its spot; stepLeaf how far one step of the march through a gap between copies may reach across the ground, in leaf clumps (smaller is smoother and costs more at a low look). season: physical albedo (linear) per season, blended through the year; flower the flowers' albedo. dormant: in season units, when it sits low and dark.
